publications.description:
Officially Endorsed Indiana Bicentennial Legacy Project 2016
In this first crowdsourced book about Indiana, ordinary Hoosiers from all corners of the state share the eclectic, wonderful, and sometimes wacky stories that are undeniably Indiana. These true tales highlight the variety of Hoosier life—fond recollections of hometowns, legendary anecdotes of the past, Indiana’s unpredictable weather, favorite foods (there’s more than corn!), and chance encounters with unforgettable and infamous people. And, of course, there’s always basketball. Written for anyone who has ever called this great state home, Undeniably Indiana provides the answer to the widespread question, “What is a Hoosier?”

headline: Lead-to-Cash Digital Transformation at Deloitte
about: As a psychology major, my career ambitions always included serving the customer, which first took form as a saleswoman, then as a marketer, and finally in digital transformation. In my role at Michelin, I leveraged my expertise in sales and marketing to solution on Salesforce.com and enhance Michelin's processes across their global digital footprint. This unique opportunity, where I learned to translate business experience into technical design, pivoted my career into consulting with Deloitte to assist other companies in achieving the digital transformations of their dreams.

experience.description: After joining Deloitte, I positioned myself where my passions lie: in Tech, Media, and Telecom. I’ve worked on three projects since joining: acting as a sales enablement lead for a cybersecurity company; a lead-to-opportunity assessment co-lead for an automated products company; and a project management co-lead for a software company. I’ve also had the opportunity to join two RFPs and co-lead the operations meetings for our Q2C business.

After seven years in B2B2C Sales and Marketing at Michelin, I moved into a Sr. Global Consultant/BA role to fulfill my long-term aspirations of leading global digital transformation at Michelin. My responsibilities included leading the cross-stream innovation and development of global lead management, piloting B2C marketing automation with global distribution partners in UAE and Asia, and acting as the regional marketing leader for Central America, South America and Europe.

After a global reorganization at Michelin, I joined a hybrid customer experiences team as the Customer Communication and Experiences Manager. In this role, I designed and implemented a successful communication strategy utilizing Salesforce.com Marketing Cloud that has tailored business communication to customers and increased our open rate by 20% YoY. Additionally, I redesigned our Advisory Councils to better utilize customer feedback and facilitate effective solution development. Some of the interesting challenges I faced included amplifying the impact of my digital activities, deepening my knowledge of the SFDC platform, further streamlining the experiences strategy to include customer feedback from advisory councils, and spearheading women's leadership initiatives to better diversify our global business teams.

experience.description:
I am a principal in the Policy and Health and Welfare practice groups at Groom Law Group, Chartered. I advise insurance companies, employers, third party administrators, trade associations, and other corporate clients on a wide range of federal tax issues affecting health and welfare plans. My passion is working closely with my clients to develop personalized legislative and regulatory strategies that advances their interests within the larger framework of sound public policy. 

I represent clients in front of key committees on Capitol Hill, the applicable Federal Agencies (Treasury, IRS, DOL, HHS, and OMB), and the White House. I have deep technical expertise in the taxation of health and welfare plans, including the “Cadillac Tax”, employer shared responsibility, the tax reporting requirements of the Internal Revenue Code sections 6055 and 6056, and premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions. I also work with cafeteria plans, tax nondiscrimination rules, fringe benefits, and VEBAs. 

My expertise extends to retirement plans, where I advise clients on executive compensation, qualified plans and pension plan funding issues.

As the Associate Benefits Tax Counsel in the Office of Tax Policy, I helped create and review policies, legislation, and regulations relating to employee benefits taxation with an emphasis on health care regulations and implementation.  I work closely with the IRS, DOL, HHS, and other Treasury officials to develop and review U.S. Treasury regulations and IRS rulings on a wide range of employee benefits issues.

As an Attorney-Advisor in the Office of Benefits Tax Counsel, I helped create and review policies, legislation, and regulations relating to employee benefits taxation with an emphasis on health care regulations and implementation.  I worked closely with the IRS, DOL, HHS, and other Treasury officials to develop and review U.S. Treasury regulations and IRS rulings on a wide range of employee benefits issues.

I served as Legislation Counsel on the staff of the Joint Committee on Taxation, a nonpartisan bicameral committee of the U.S. Congress.  While working for JCT I was involved in a number of legislative projects including the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009, and the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008.  In addition to working on legislation, I helped prepare written explanations of pending legislation and current law on topics ranging from executive compensation, to pension funding, to the taxation of health care.

headline: Senior Data Science Consultant at Deloitte

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

about: I am a data scientist motivated by the need for consistent growth and I am always looking for a new challenge.  My background in analytics, combined with my passion for using data to solve problems, allows me to quickly apply logic to uncover any possible areas for improvement. I want to bring these skills to organizations with cultures that value corporate social responsibility.

experience.description:
• Completed 25 labs in Jupyter Notebooks to practice and solve challenging data science problems in order to master necessary libraries and become self-sufficient in Python and statistical data analysis

• Students completed 6 projects requiring us to acquire, clean, and analyze datasets and use data visualization tools to present findings to non-technical audiences:
     - Improving SAT Participation Rates: EDA and data visualizations using Numpy, Pandas, Seaborn, and Matplotlib in order to combine and convert 6 datasets of SAT/ACT scores and participation. The final recommendation to the College Board was that consistent evaluation and improvement of free SAT prep is vital to increasing participation.
     - Housing Price Predictions: Analyzed more than 70 columns of housing data resulting with a linear regression model in Scikit-Learn that explained 84% of the variance in Sale Price, tested significance values of feature coefficients to determine which to include. Used grid-search/pipelines to experiment with Scaling numerical data, One Hot Encoding categorical data, and Polynomial Features.
     - Subreddit Classification with NLP: Used web scraping to pull posts from two subreddits (r/Jokes vs. r/riddles) and NLP to breakdown contents of posts into usable data with Lemmatization and CountVectorizer. The classifier model correctly identified the subreddits with 88% accuracy. Areas for improvement: data cleaning to remove deleted posts and create a new feature of the entire post (title, text, comments).
     - Image Classification Translator: Built an image classification model using neural networks, resulting in 86% accuracy classifying 30 words and translated into 107 languages. Presented to a non-technical audience with comprehensible, succinct slides that explained decision points and results; created a Streamlit app to demonstrate translator functionality. Areas for improvement: add more words to app and allow usage with live video through object detection.

• Used market research and experimented with promotional strategies to set pricing for 8,000 market rate units at 32 properties in collaboration with leasing agents in New York, California, and Chicago; met weekly with buildings’ property staff to discuss balance of ~2% increase in rental rate each year and consistent occupancy at 98%

• Created new process to predict, track, and analyze digital advertising expenditure ROI (Google, Streeteasy, and Internet Listing Services) by pulling invoice data from Hubble, click throughs on Google Analytics, and Salesforce inquiries/leases; resulted in savings of $1.1M YoY, increased insight into cost per click, and understanding of spending efficiency

• Designed, monitored, and delivered reports daily during the pandemic to guide the decision-making of upper management and investors related to pricing, advertising, promotions, and debt collection; part of a successful initiative to keep teams equally informed, creating the ability to pivot quickly and catch problems before they arise

• Tasked with new problem of $6M unpaid rent each month due to pandemic job loss; used Excel to create user-friendly dashboard that allowed site managers and corporate staff to communicate updates while reviewing daily inputs of payment and occupancy data, leading to collections of 98% by the end of year

• Owned budget process for 40+ Luxury Portfolio properties: yearly efforts to provide efficient templates by reviewing pain points and successes of previous year with key stakeholders, training and technical support for property managers, and presentation of company-wide business plan to management; worked closely with a team of 1-2 people per department (Marketing, Engineering, Finance, and Accounting) organized with Gantt charts and weekly meetings

• Implemented a performance-based bonus structure for site staff in Excel using measurable metrics of the property (renewal rate, occupancy, variance to budget) and of the employee (performance evaluation and resident surveys); resulting in a reproducible template that continues to be used years later, making the process fair and cost effective

• Determined the value of an internal Call Center using large datasets containing call volume per hour/day, voicemails, and appointments booked; outcome helped to better position the Call Center staff at properties that needed the service

• Designed a three-tier resident loyalty program to offer gifts to tenants; process included evaluating drop off points in renewal rates and determining gifts to offer that were of no cost to the company (free amenities, parking, etc); program was unsuccessful and surveys showed that tenants would prefer to be awarded discounts on rent

• Complete 4-6 State Reviews each year by gathering and analyzing large sets of Salesforce data in Qlikview and Excel in order to determine best pricing strategy to promote growth and profitability by targeting key groups within a state; gained experience presenting to all executives while developing deep understanding of numbers and analytics 

• Developed Homeowners Discount for all direct new business by collecting quantitative data from Salesforce and anecdotal data from Sales team, pitched proposal to department managers, and worked with IT/Marketing to implement in 15 states; began tracking results after 6 months and saw a sales increase of 8%

• Selected as one of five participants for GE’s premier rotational program that involved contributing to multiple roles
     - Accounting & Investments Analyst: Created a successful Accounts Payable process improvement by creating a form to enter incoming checks that had previously been done manually; assisted CFO and Finance team monitoring current investments while evaluating opportunities for growth; gained detailed understanding of business needs/goals
     - Personal Lines Product Analyst: Responsible for User Acceptance Testing while migrating company data into Qlikview in order to develop interactive analytics applications and dashboards; developed skill for attention to detail and introduction to coding

•	Reformatted  the Response Library - a data mart for the analytics team, where the company memorializes response data for clients, by category, with an eye to in-market data, such as pricing and offer
•	Executed use of the Response Library by utilizing historical response data to examine trends and analyze client performance across different products and executions; presented findings to the VP of Analytics

experience.description: Motivated by a dissatisfaction with GDP as the sole measure of a nation's status, I spearheaded a global effort to establish a think tank focused on the concept of Total Value. Our team explored the intersections of Money, Data, Sentiment, and Ideology to forecast a new transnational "currency" that would be more inclusive and representative than traditional fiscal values. Our work not only fostered a deeper understanding of the Metaverse, but also highlighted the potential of 4th Industrial Revolution Technologies such as Blockchain (4IR), AI, IoT, and 5G in creating an ecosystem that captures Total Value.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, I actively contributed to the 'Masks Without Borders' campaign by assisting in the distribution of masks across Chicago. In collaboration with various non-profit organisations, we aimed to distribute a total of 10,000 masks to those in need. As part of my role, I worked closely with local media to raise awareness of the campaign and drafted articles, emails, and call scripts to expand the foundation's network. Additionally, I organised grassroots fundraising events to further support the foundation's efforts. Through my contributions, I was able to play a role in helping to keep the community safe during a challenging time.

headline: Senior Salesforce Consultant @Deloitte | 7x Salesforce Certified
about:
After launching my career as a Salesforce Consultant in Madrid (Spain) in 2017, I moved to USA looking for exciting career opportunities. Since then, I have learned (and am still learning) from the best firms and clients in the world.

From analyzing complex business processes to implementing high-efficiency solutions, my focus has always been on delivering maximum stakeholder value while placing our clients at the forefront of technology.

experience.description:
- Banking & Financial Services: Governance program to improve alignment and standardization across the organization's CRM team.

Activities: Helped share visibility on status of work against enterprise funds, tackle key business-related challenges and established business priorities together with business executives. Help anticipate on risks and dependencies between lines of businesses through alignment meetings. Analyze the preparedness for upcoming development cycles and data integrity through new Dashboards and Reports

Results: Successfully built a governance structure that brings standardization and alignment throughout the enterprise CRM team. Established a stronger Salesforce COE model with the creation of artifacts and practical documentation.

Results: Effectively drove quality and minimized substantial legal, financial, and reputational risk. Our efforts digitally transformed the customer journey saving a significant time per deal, improving contract execution velocity and increasing delivery volume.

- Leading Automotive Manufacturer: Worldwide digital transformation of all Salesforce Marketing, Sales and Service activities throughout the different manufacturing brands and countries.

Role: Functional Lead for Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, KPIs and Reporting

Activities: Leading a Team of 10+ Consultants and developers. Facilitating meetings during Sprints, Requirement Gathering with POs and Solution Leads, Sprint plannings and estimations, Scope definition, Resource allocation, JIRA maintenance, Retrospective sessions, supervision of technical and functional solutions, Project Management activities, Coordination with stakeholders and partners. Impact made: 24 Releases/Year. Platform extended to all European dealers, both in daily commercial operative and customer service. Reduction of interfaces and optimization of existing integrations. Centralized monitoring of end-to-end process.

Metrics: 16 Brands. 24 Countries. +42.000 Users impacted. +54M Clients.

Main challenges: Merge of two OEM groups into one, Online Selling, New Retailer Model, process adaptation for each country and brand, Fleet Sales process definition, managing data across multiple clouds and stages, coordinating releases in a multi-partner project.

headline: Tax Partner at Deloitte
about:
I am a Partner and lead the International Tax Practice for our Chicago office.  I serve clients in a variety of industries including consumer products, financial services, technology, and manufacturing.  I work with multinational corporations on a wide variety of international tax issues, including earnings repatriation, cross-border financing, foreign tax credit planning, Pillar II assessments, and foreign country tax reduction with an emphasis on value chain alignment strategies.

I am a Certified Public Accountant, a member of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants, and hold a Bachelors of Science and a Masters of Science in Accountancy from the University of Illinois in Champaign-Urbana.  I have been a guest lecturer at the University of Illinois Masters in Tax Program.  I have presented on various international tax topics for BNA/CITE.

I have served as an ambassador to the United Way, volunteer for Ladder Up and FMSC, and am a Mentor for Big Brothers Big Sisters.  My most important job title is "Dad" from my two sons (Cole and Reed) and daughter (Lena).

Specialties: Tax Planning, Private Equity, Hedge Funds, Mutual Funds, Asset Management, Value Chain Alignment, Supply Chain Restructuring, Cash Repatriation, Cross-Border Financing, ASC 740, Pillar II.

headline: Global Trade Advisory | Manager - Deloitte Tax LLP
about:
My name is Gabriela M. Heizer. I am an international trade professional with experience in import and export laws, regulations, and compliance. 

I am a licensed attorney in the State of Illinois, having graduated with my Juris Doctor from University of Illinois Chicago. During that time, I focused on international trade law and international human rights law, gaining invaluable experience through internships and clinic work. I am also a Florida Atlantic University Alumna with a Bachelors in International Business and Trade. 

As a native of Brazil, I grew up in two different cultures and appreciate the importance of international business and international trade, which is why I focus in this area. My experience in international trade law began in law school during my time with TK Trade Law as a legal intern. During that internship, I was able to do legal research on client specific trade questions via statutory research, Customs Regulations, and CBP Rulings. I’ve dealt with issues such as: First Sale Rule, USMCA, country of origin, valuation, tariff classification, and Section 301 tariff exclusions. I have also lead clients in the CTPAT compliance. Currently at FTI Consulting, I assist companies in implementing programs such as CTPAT and Foreign Trade Zones, conducting third-party screenings, and creating written procedures to comply with new trade regulations. 

Further, I have worked as a 711-Student Attorney at UIC School of Law's International Human Rights Clinic. In this clinic, I worked directly with asylum seekers and helped them prepare their asylum applications. This has given me valuable experience with client communication and interviews. I have also developed precise attention to detail while preparing client applications.

experience.description: Global Trade Advisory Manager
Export Control, Sanctions, and Trade Practice
Export Control, Sanctions, and Trade Practice

During my time at TK Trade Law I drafted memoranda answering trade questions via statutory research, Customs Regulations, and the CBP Rulings. I further conducted research on a range of issues including, but not limited to, First Sale Rule, USMCA, Drawback, county of origin, Section 301 tariff exclusions, and U.S. origin statements. I also participated in internal investigations of companies and prepared a benchmark survey study.

I worked with the International Trade Law group at Modine Manufacturing. I participated in meetings with Brazil to implement new LGPD compliance and draft new written procedures and lead companies in Mexico with C-TPAT and AEO programs to facilitate compliance with U.S. trade regulations. I also assisted with ITAR registration by communicating with global subsidiaries. On an ongoing basis, I conducted third-party screenings to identify potential risks third-party may present.

In the summer of 2020, in the middle of the pandemci, my friends and I worked hard to create something we are truly passionate about. We’d like to introduce you to Generation Now Foundation. Generation Now Foundation seeks to level the playing field for first-generation students seeking post-graduate careers. We aim to provide representation, resources, and resilience. Our website is up and running with resources that can be used TODAY! Check it out at generationnowfoundation.org

experience.description:

reports like – People Insights, Shopper Insights, Brand Insights, New Item Insights and

aim to get various valuable information regarding the promotion impact, purchase planning, 
store or brand shifting, etc.

useful insights and suggestions to clients.

Also looking into training of new hires and enhanced process as per requirement of the dept.

publications.title: Impact of Personality Types and Matching Messaging on Password Strength
publications.description: People often create passwords for their accounts that are insecure. An insecure password is often easy to guess– thus, hackers can easily access their victims’ accounts. It is important for users to know how to create and manage secure passwords so they can better protect themselves from hackers. It is well-known that different users have different personality types, such as Big Five and True Colors. This research examines if there is any link between personality types and password security behavior. Each participant was shown either a matching or mismatching message based on their personality type, and it was measured whether their password security behavior changed a month later. Our results show that 66% of participants with a Green (knowledgeable and competent) personality type chose a strong password, compared to less than 50% of other personality types. Our results also demonstrate that messaging has a statistical impact on improving password security behavior.

projects.title: U.S. RESPONSE TO THE REFUGEE CRISIS:  THE CASE FOR STRATEGIC REALLOCATION OF FUNDS AND INCREASED TRANSPARENCY
projects.description:
Conducted a qualitative and quantitative analysis of U.S. government's current refugee resettlement policy, procedures, and management in light of the Syrian Refugee Crisis. The team met and consulted with stakeholders in Washington D.C. from several organizations such as: State Department, Department of Health and Human Services, Ridge Policy Group, Brookings Institute, George Mason University, and Refugees International. Major contribution was the development of several models to identify and forecast trends in funding and costs for the Refugee Admissions Program.

The report provides 6 recommendations:
1. Increase the transparency of the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program by including detailed information about program expenses—to include administrative, overhead, programmatic, and grant expenses- and additional details of the refugee screening and resettlement process in the annual report to Congress.
2. Increase the transparency of the interagency role of the National Security Council in the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program so that journalists, advocacy organizations, and the general public can have a greater understanding of how these important decisions are made.
3. Exercise selectivity and strategic planning to reallocate U.S. funds for UNHCR’s country programs from which the largest number of refugees are resettled.
4. Reevaluate the methodology for calculating federal funding and allocation criteria for refugee resettlement (PRM’s R&P program and ORR’s Matching Grants) to alleviate some of the financial burden on NGO partners.
5. Build flexibility into the clearance process by developing a risk threshold for discrete changes in refugees’ profile data that compares the potential delays to the associated security risk.
6. Offer the PRM-funded guidebook Welcome to the United States: A Guidebook for Refugees in more languages spoken by refugees, especially those coming from countries where the U.S. has ongoing military and strategic diplomatic commitments.

experience.description: After serving as treasurer, I was elected to president for the team. As president, I was responsible for scheduling the games for the team, organizing the team activities and managing the relationship between the team and the school. I also pushed the team in new directions by being part of more events outside of our normal season. The biggest impact I left behind was the creation of a new organizational structure. I felt there were inefficiencies in the team and I worked to fix those by adding a second treasurer, a fundraising director, and an event coordinator. These additions improved the team's ability to have a successful season on and off the field.

In 2016, I served as the treasurer for men's club soccer. I handled all three of the financial dimensions the team faced, being fund management, collection and expenditure. I created a budget and filed it with the Associated Student Government to obtain school funding for the team. I collected tryout fees, team member dues and setup a donation portal to provide additional funding. I paid for all team expenses through Miami University's internal software, including travel expenses, referee payments, field rental fees and any other purchases that were necessary to make the season successful. The team took part in away games throughout Ohio, a regional tournament in Indiana and a national tournament in Alabama. As the gatekeeper of the team funds, I was heavily involved with the planning of this travel to make sure it fit in the budget. At the conclusion of my term, the outgoing president asked me to run for team president. I was elected and transitioned into that position for 2017.

As a member of Phi Chi Theta at Miami University, I worked on the professional committee. My role required me to be knowledgeable about what employers value so that I could advise other members how to craft a successful resume, find valuable experiences to engage in and communicate with companies in a professional manner. I also helped to plan the professional trips that the business fraternity takes each semester, which included organizing visits with various companies.

From the end of my sophomore year to the beginning of my senior year, I served as the archon of my fraternity, Pi Kappa Phi. In Pi Kappa Phi, the archon acts as the chapter president and is responsible for all of the fraternity's operations. When I took over the chapter, the leaders that came before me had made some poor decisions and had caused the chapter to lose its recognition at Miami University. Because of this, I was tasked with rebuilding the fraternity. I had to communicate and collaborate extensively with the national organization, the alumni association, and the school to work towards the new expectations facing the chapter. I led the chapter through a series of sanctions, positioned it to be desirable to new members and returned it to a normal operating level. In the end, the chapter went from 27 remaining members when I took over to 89 members when I finished my second term in the role. The improvement I am most proud of was the philanthropic work completed by the chapter. The leadership before me had neglected that facet of the chapter, and I was able to bring it back with the help of many dedicated members. The chapter went from $0 raised the year before I took over and ended up raising $11,833 for The Ability Experience, an organization dedicated to improving the lives of people with disabilities. Overall, this position added the most to my college career as I was able to experience how to turn a struggling organization around, which I feel was a very rare opportunity in college.

She also leads due diligence teams to advise some of Deloitte’s most significant private equity and strategic buyer clients on M&A transactions.  Ayesha is a member of Deloitte's Board Council and the M&A Executive Committee. Based in Chicago, Ayesha joined Deloitte in 1995 and became a partner in 2007. 

Ayesha focuses on consumer products and retail industries. She led Deloitte's US Advisory Practice for Consumer Products and Deloitte's National Retail, Wholesale and Distribution M&A Transaction Services practice. 

With over 29 years of experience with Deloitte, including over 21 years in the M&A Transaction Services group, Ayesha has assisted clients on 200+ transactions ranging in size from $10 million to $38 billion across the globe. 

Ayesha is highly regarded for her client service excellence and is committed to delivering the insights clients need to address their most critical and complex business challenges related to acquisitions and divestitures.  She has extensive experience in complex carve-out transactions advising both sellers and buyers, including assisting clients with the preparation of financial statements, pro forma financial information and other information included in regulatory filings. 

Ayesha graduated from the McIntire School of Commerce at the University of Virginia and is a member of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA).

slides.title: What could M&A look like this year? The vaccine and latest holiday shopping season data may hold clues
slides.subtitle: Ayesha Rafique on LinkedIn
slides.description: What could M&A look like this year? The vaccine and latest holiday shopping season data may hold clues By Ayesha Rafique Considering the year we all had, I think its safe to say everyone is hopeful for a better 2021. This is certainly the case for my industry, where optimism around M&A improved over the course of the year, with 61% of surveyed dealmakers estimating that US M&A activity could return to pre-COVID-19 levels within 12 months. I would even argue that dealmaking optimism is on the rise yet again thanks to the positive stream of vaccine news and developments that pepper today’s news headlines. Of course, much remains to be seen in terms of how M&A will shape up once the world returns to a more normal operating environment. While deal volume will likely normalize at some point in the near-to-medium term, we’ve seen other dealmaking trends emerge that could signal a new era of how deals get done. Chief among those trends is an interest among 55% of surveyed dealmakers to adopt entirely virtual deal rooms moving forward, thanks in part to 87% reporting success at effectively managing deals in a purely virtual environment. Anecdotally, I can tell you that many dealmakers I speak with are eager to get back to in-person dealmaking once it’s safe, but time will tell just how sticky this trend will be. With increased interest in virtual deal rooms and near-term M&A growth, we saw a resurgence of dealmaking in Q3 and Q41 and may find some clues as to why by taking a closer look at the consumer industry as an example. Many looked to the 2020 shopping season as a make-or-break moment for survival after tough sales data for the majority of last year. Heading into the holiday season, predictions weren’t great: the average household spend expectation was down 7% year-over-year mostly due to economic instability, with in-store shopping further threatened by a clear preference for offsite purchases (e.g., delivery/73% and curbside pick-up/27%) due to anxiety about shopping in-store affecting 51% of consumers. The latest numbers confirm this disappointing trend, with retail sales revised downward recently to -1.4% for November (from an initially reported -1.1%) and December sales down 0.7%. So, what does this potentially mean for dealmaking? Private equity (PE) investors are likely more on edge coming out of the 2020 holiday season, especially since the retail businesses they own tend to have more debt on their books compared to non-PE-backed peers. Their focus now is to rework that debt in anticipation of worsening fundamentals that may have materialized for some businesses as a result of the poor holiday shopping season. The result could be a moderation of some near-term M&A plans in an effort to strengthen balance sheets – through cost reduction to improve margins, liquidity management, working capital optimization, asset sales, exits/store closures, and PE lending – for future deals or potentially focus on Chapter 11 restructurings. For other retailers, the lack of in-store traffic is likely to just be a temporary setback that won’t meaningfully derail financials—the pandemic has, after all, disproportionately affected the industry, boosting some shopping segments and not others. Yet, even with a vaccine now in distribution, the timeline for vaccinating the majority of the public will be lengthy, meaning that the normalization of store traffic is likely still some ways off. The retailers that fall into this category (i.e., those not in immediate distress) are generally looking at whether they can change their business models through non-traditional M&A, another significant trend we saw in 2020, and which could continue to play out this year for all industries. While the 2020 holiday season may have been rife with creative partnerships and joint ventures—such as store-in-store alliances—these are not holiday-driven trends. Generally, many factors would need to change for alternative M&A approaches like creative partnerships and special purpose acquisition companies to fully reverse, especially considering that there are strategic reasons to explore non-traditional strategies that are not dependent on economic stress. Many corporates also now prefer alternative approaches over all other dealmaking strategies, which could help drive sustained interest in them. If anything, the more business moves in a positive direction, the better potential for a slight retrenchment in alternative dealmaking this year, driven perhaps by the fact that PE investors still largely prefer traditional acquisitions. The consumer industry is certainly not a bellwether for the M&A world, but provides a glimpse at what could be in store for this year. Many companies across industries remain cautiously optimistic about the vaccine’s effect on the operating landscape and, barring no other major hiccups in the recovery process, I’m hopeful that there may be a continued hold onto some of the emerging dealmaking trends of 2020—virtual dealmaking and alternative acquisitions—and see M&A return to pre-COVID-19 levels by the end of 2021. 1 Deloitte Future of M&A Trends Survey, October 2020 About Deloitte Deloitte refers to one or more of Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited, a UK private company limited by guarantee (“DTTL”), its network of member firms, and their related entities. Amala is a Associate Director with over 13 years of experience in providing financial statement and internal control assurance services. She specializes in information security audit and has been involved with reviewing various IT environments within the Consumer business and telecommunications, Energy and Resources, and Financial Services industries.
She has led and managed teams that performed systems audit, internal audit review for blue-chip companies. She has also been involved in extensive data quality and integrity review using Computer Assisted Audit Tools for several Enterprise Resources Planning ’ERP’ application environments.
She has performed security reviews for a number of financial applications/ERP (SAP, Oracle Application, Lawson, Flexcube, Finacle etc.), Operating Systems (Windows, UNIX (AIX, Solaris and True 64) and AS/400) and Databases (Oracle. Microsoft SQL and SQL Database). She has also been involved in testing controls around data conversion process and interfaces configurations.
Amala participated in Deloitte’s Global Development Program between February 2011 and September 2013, where she was seconded to The United States of America. Here, she served a wide range of clients in the Deloitte Chicago office and gained extensive knowledge in IT Audits, Integrated Audits, Risk Assessments, ERP Security and Controls, and Data Analytics. She also attended several trainings on Internal Controls over Financial Reporting, ERP Packages and Risk Assessments.
She has been instrumental in building capabilities through developing team winning strategies and executing them brilliantly. She has also assisted in developing core competencies and talents.
She is passionate about what she does and is notable for instilling good team spirit amongst her team members and has demonstrated the ability to put out fires and maintain team morale. Amala is very goal oriented and diligently works to achieve defined targets.

headline: Manager  | Sustainability Compliance Reporting
about:
I am a curious, ambitious, and analytical professional honing an expertise in accounting, strategy, and sustainability. Through my actions both in my work and my personal life, I strive to promote a more sustainable and socially just world.

Currently, I am a Manager in Deloitte's internal reporting practice with a focus on sustainability compliance reporting. I will be responsible for the development, implementation, and management of Deloitte's ESG compliance reporting framework, working closely with various stakeholders to drive Deloitte's sustainability agenda. 

Before joining Deloitte, I served public and private clients in Grant Thornton’s ESG & Sustainability practice in the areas of materiality assessments, climate risk assessments, greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory management plans (IMPs), assurance readiness, and limited and reasonable assurance. I also developed a subject matter expert in Europe’s Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and its European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS). I produced educational materials on the CSRD, actively participated in a multi-accounting-firm group that discussed complex or unclear accounting issues with the goal of consistently interpreting and applying the ESRS, and advised clients on how they will be affected by and can prepare for the CSRD.

Additionally, I served both public and private clients for four years as a member of KPMG’s and EY's assurance practices. My previous experience consists of leading  integrated audits under PCAOB standards and financial statement audits under AICPA standards. My industry experience includes manufacturing, pharmaceutical, bio-tech, utilities, and professional services industries.

I hold a B.S. in Accountancy from Boston College and an active Ohio CPA license and AICPA membership. I have also completed training programs with the GHG Protocol and the TCFD.

profileTopEducation.schoolName: Boston College - Wallace E. Carroll Graduate School of Management

experience.description:
As a Manager in Sustainability Compliance Reporting, I will play a critical role in ensuring Deloitte meets its environmental, social, and governance (ESG) regulatory reporting obligations. I will be responsible for the development, implementation, and management of Deloitte's ESG compliance reporting framework, working closely with various stakeholders to drive Deloitte's sustainability agenda. 

My specific responsibilities include:
- Lead the development and execution of the ESG compliance reporting strategy, ensuring alignment with regulatory standards and stakeholder expectations.
- Manage the collection, analysis, and reporting of ESG data across the organization.
- Oversee the preparation of comprehensive ESG reports for internal and external stakeholders, including regulatory bodies and investors.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate ESG considerations into business operations and decision-making processes.
- Monitor and assess changes in ESG regulations and reporting standards, ensuring the firm remains compliant.
- Provide training and support to staff on ESG compliance and reporting requirements.
- Develop and maintain relationships with external stakeholders, including regulatory agencies and industry organizations.
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of ESG reporting processes.

As a Manager in Grant Thornton's ESG & Sustainability practice, I continued to work on assurance readiness engagements, limited assurance engagements, and other projects that developed my subject matter expertise - with a focus on CSRD engagements. My promotion to manager primarily represents a change in mindset from being a 'doer' to a 'reviewer' and 'manager'. 

The responsibilities of a this role include: Business development, budgeting, staffing, billing, mentoring and training, internal and external communication, and quality reviewing action plans, workpapers, and deliverables.

As a Senior Associate in Grant Thornton's ESG & Sustainability practice, I transformed my financial reporting mindset and work experience into an expertise in sustainability reporting, with a specialization in the CSRD. My work highlights include:

CSRD Scoping -- I independently researched the CSRD in order to understand the scoping element of the directive, and then I developed a methodology for Grant Thornton to perform this service for its clients. I performed this service for a publishing company and a chemicals and materials company.

Assurance Readiness -- Clients look to Grant Thornton's deep corporate reporting expertise and perspective as an independent assurance provider for assistance in complying with complex regulations or unfamiliar reporting frameworks. We walkthrough processes, perform limited testing procedures over disclosed data, and assess the draft disclosures against the reporting framework, and we provide a list of observations and recommendations in relation to the sufficiency of reported disclosures, processes, control environment, quality of reported data, and documentation maintained. I led teams of 1-2 individuals to provide this service for a professional services company preparing for its initial CSRD report, a medical devices company for its initial double materiality assessment, and a biotech company preparing to comply with the GHG Protocol.

Limited Assurance -- I lead teams of 1-2 individuals to perform limited assurance over environmental and social metrics (primarily GHG scopes 1, 2, and 3 metrics) for a tire distribution company, a datacenter company, and a manufacturing company.

Other projects include: Publishing educational materials on the CSRD and the SEC climate rule, producing and presenting CPE trainings related to ESG regulations and the GHG Protocol, and contributing to a multi-accounting-firm group that discusses complex or unclear accounting issues with the goal of consistently interpreting and applying the ESRS.

I was engaged to work with EY as a contractor at the Audit Senior Associate level for August 2021 - April 2022. During my time with EY, I held the role of a lead senior for two international statutory audits of a SAAS company and of an Assisting Senior for a utilities provider audit and a security services audit.

My work includes the following:
- Using critical thinking when assessing prior period procedures and developing an audit plan for the current period
- Guiding staff - developing daily / weekly tasks and providing feedback
- Detail reviewing audit documentation of EY staff to meet EY audit standards
- Implementing the use of an EY Digital GL Analysis audit tool, which allowed us to reduce our PPE sample size from 350 selections to 31
- Leading the audit effort for a tax reserve of a significant business acquisition
- Leading meetings with the client and EY managers
- Adapting quickly to new audit clients to be able to provide assistance to audit teams for short periods of time

I utilized my experience from KPMG as well as my business education and CPA to provide internal accounting assistance to a multi-national fitness company. I worked with several members of the US and Australian accounting teams. My main project was to assist the company in its transition from Xero to NetSuite, which involved a great deal of historical data reformatting and reconciliations between the records of the two systems. 

My work included:
- Historical Invoice Analysis
- Month-End Reconciliation or Analysis of Specific Accounts
- Data Mapping of Historical Information
- Reconciliation between Legacy Reporting Systems and New Systems

As a senior associate, my role on the engagement team was to develop an audit plan with the manager and partner and to execute the plan efficiently and effectively by leading the other team members, communicating with the client, and delivering a quality product following by incorporating review from the manager and partner. 

I held the role of the lead senior associate for a private education company under PCAOB standards, a newly public biotech company, a few employee benefit plans, and a component audit of a private manufacturing company under IFRS standards.

Skills I focused on developing as a senior include: 
- Engagement management
- Effective risk assessment (process understanding, planning analytics, and significant account scoping)
- Technical accounting expertise

As an audit associate, I developed an understanding of the audit process by working on the FY17 and FY18 audits of a public, vertically integrated health care company. During the FY 18 audit, beginning in August 2018, I held a senior level role on the team, in charging the pharmacy and manufacturing division of the audit. I was the main point of contact to the client, worked directly with the manager, and kept my team (additional 1-2 associates) on track to complete all audit procedures from the risk assessment phase through the substantive phase.

Also as an audit associate with KPMG, I also worked on the IPOs of two life science clients, quarterly reviews for public and private companies under PCAOB standards, employee benefit plans, and audits of two first year clients.

education.description:
I studied abroad during the fall semester of my Junior Year at the Copenhagen Business School in Copenhagen, Denmark. Two unique classes I took were The Economics of the Euro and Event and Festival Management. While abroad, I also had the opportunity to travel to eight countries around Europe and to really get to know the city of Copenhagen. 

If you are in Copenhagen for a weekend, three of the things I would recommend that you do are: (1) Rent a bike and ride around the city. The buildings all over the city are beautiful, it is very easy and safe to ride around the city, and you can see much more of it by bike than by foot. (2) Eat at Papirøen. Translated as "Paper Island", the warehouse on this island used to store the paper used by the Danish Press. It has recently, and temporarily, been turned into a multi-cultural street food market. (3) Go to Tivoli Gardens at night. Tivoli is an old, classic, and beautiful amusement park, which happened to also inspire Walt Disney's Disneyland.

University School helped me develop a drive for academic excellence, an understanding of financial markets, and a love of competition.

During my tenure at the US Food and Drug Administration, Division of Food Contact Notifications, I contributed to the modernization of food safety assessments by leveraging computational toxicology and change management strategies. My work centered on developing advanced tools and methodologies to evaluate the safety of food contact substances, integrating data-driven approaches to enhance regulatory decision-making and operational efficiency.

Key Achievements:
• Collaborated on the development and refinement of computational toxicology tools, utilizing chemoinformatics, gene toxicity analysis, and carcinogenicity studies to assess the safety of new food contact materials.
• Designed and managed toxicological databases, ensuring accurate data integration and accessibility for regulatory review and scientific analysis.

Implemented and tested predictive algorithms for toxicity screening, improving the speed and consistency of safety assessments.
• Facilitated change management initiatives by training team members on new computational workflows and promoting the adoption of innovative assessment tools within the division.
• Developed standard operating procedures (SOPs) for computational toxicology processes, supporting regulatory compliance and continuous improvement.
• Coordinated cross-functional teams to integrate computational methods into existing review pipelines, streamlining the evaluation process for food contact notifications.
• Presented findings and recommendations to scientific and regulatory stakeholders, translating complex toxicological data into actionable insights for policy and decision-making.
• Monitored emerging trends in computational toxicology and regulatory science, ensuring the division remained at the forefront of scientific innovation.

experience.position: Computational Toxicology Database Manager - Leadscope Inc.
experience.description:
During my collaboration with Leadscope Inc. at the US Food and Drug Administration, I played a pivotal role in advancing computational toxicology capabilities for regulatory safety assessments. My work focused on integrating cutting-edge informatics tools and data management strategies to enhance the prediction and evaluation of toxicological risks associated with chemical substances in food contact materials. This experience allowed me to bridge scientific research, data science, and regulatory compliance, contributing to the FDA’s mission of ensuring public health and safety.

Key Achievements:
• Constructed a comprehensive, searchable toxicology database by systematically linking active chemical structures to gene toxicity results, sub-chronic and chronic exposure histories, and reproductive-developmental toxicity data, enabling more robust safety assessments.
• Interpreted and synthesized complex in vivo and in vitro study results, managing large toxicological data sets to support the expansion of clinical databases and inform regulatory decisions.
• Collaborated in the development and refinement of proprietary software tools designed to predict the toxicity of novel chemical substances, leveraging machine learning and chemoinformatics approaches.
• Developed data curation protocols and quality control measures to ensure the integrity and reliability of toxicological databases.
• Contributed to the validation and testing of predictive algorithms, supporting the FDA’s efforts to adopt innovative, data-driven approaches in regulatory toxicology.
• Presented technical findings and recommendations to FDA leadership, supporting policy development and the adoption of advanced computational methods in regulatory practice.
• Monitored advancements in computational toxicology and championed the integration of innovative methodologies and best practices to enhance the agency’s scientific and regulatory capabilities.

As a research specialist in ecological genetics, I contributed to advancing sustainable pest management and biodiversity initiatives through comprehensive gene and phenotypic analyses. My work focused on understanding the genetic and ecological dynamics of native species and their interactions, utilizing advanced analytical techniques to generate actionable insights for both scientific research and practical policy development. I played a key role in supporting research and development efforts by maintaining critical genetic databases and providing expertise in species identification and ecological balance.

Key Achievements:
• Performed in-depth gene and phenotypic analyses to evaluate the impact of pesticides on the reproduction and fecundity of native spider mite species, as well as on predator/prey relationships within local ecosystems.
• Utilized advanced analytical methods to derive insights that guided the creation of sustainable pest management strategies and promoted ecological balance.
• Conducted preliminary genetic speciation analyses of newly identified parasitoid wasps and their hosts, enhancing the understanding of species interactions and contributing to biodiversity research.
• Applied genetic analysis techniques to identify and characterize new species, directly supporting the organization’s research and development objectives.
• Maintained and managed a comprehensive gene repository database encompassing hundreds of species, ensuring precise documentation of gene sequencing, gene expression data, and SAS statistical analyses from both field and laboratory studies.
• Provided analytical support and subject matter expertise to inform the development of sustainable pest management practices and policies, leveraging findings from genetic and phenotypic studies to drive evidence-based decision-making.

headline: Integrator, People Leader: Risk and Advisory - Internal Auditor at Deloitte & Touche
about:
There are countless titles in my life, each with their own stories and lessons that contribute to the person I am today. From a manager, innovator, and mentor to mother, wife, and optimist there are innumerable labels that describe me best. Growing up in a blended family, our dynamic represented that of a passionate, diverse, and supportive team, and I have always been devoted and motivated by this team. Transitioning into the business world, over fourteen years ago, I have brought that same mentality and devotion to my work which has fostered an amazing career I am so proud of. 
 
At Deloitte, I am working hands on with passionate, diverse, and creative individuals that inspire me each day. Being a part of a team my whole life, I know the importance of inclusion, empathy, and different perspectives. I strive to bring people together and ensure that those I work with feel supported. I am devoted to diversity, equity and inclusion culture and have created initiatives nationally across the Deloitte firm. Through my optimistic mindset, I am apart of many successful teams that bring internal audit services to some of the largest and most complex clients in the financial industry. 
 
As an optimist, I am always looking for a solution. If something doesn’t work, it’s okay, we will find an answer. I enjoy looking at life from a glass half pull perspective. My desire to solve problems provided me the opportunity to be a Senior Manager on Deloitte’s  Internal Audit Innovation team which identifies and creates new solutions for internal auditing. I’m on the forefront of technology and innovation and I am inspired by the work we do. 
 
I bring my perspective and titles to all aspects of my life. Whether it’s leading meetings or spending a summer day in Michigan with my three kids and husband, my upbeat personality is always there. Life is always full of challenges but it’s important to remember you get what you get and make the best of it. I am eager to see what comes next!

about:
Sydney has over ten years of experience in health care and life sciences, across military health, health plan, provider, and pharma. She is passionate about understanding human and consumer needs, transforming business processes, and building equitable solutions that meet both human and business goals, all in an effort to streamline and make health care more approachable and accessible. She has been effective in leading multi-dimentional teams in journey mapping, data analysis, health equity anc customer strategy development, workshopping, and facilitation. Sydney’s interests include graphic facilitation, meeting facilitation, data visualization, and equity-centered design. As Manager of Cloud Business Operations, Noemi is committed to improving business relationships with customers and partners while strengthening solidarity within business service teams.  

Noemi is dedicated to efficiently addressing growing business needs, among them:
* Improving business processes related to contract onboarding, quarterly business review and disaster recovery tests and role swap efforts.  
* Establishing new services and add-on services through managing and coordinating teams of cloud resources and project managers.
* Obtaining high customer satisfaction levels and increased service renewals by successfully managing clients and end-users.
* Strategically strengthening data centers and subscription software vendor relationships through the addition of services, negotiation of rates and approval of payment requisitions.

As the Project Manager for the Cloud Services Division of Meridian IT, Noemi is involved in multiple aspects of the cloud business group.  On the presales front of the hosting business, Noemi is engaged in the discussion of client’s service needs and environment configurations/setups.  In addition, she executes hosting contracts and is involved in client negotiations for changes in the contract.  On the post sales end the hosting business, as the central point of contact, Noemi processes signed hosting agreements and drives the onboarding of all hosting services.  Upon the completion of onboarding of services, she maintains frequent communication with hosting clients and assists with annual and miscellaneous service requests.

With a quickly expanding annuity services division at Meridian IT and two (2) data center facilities, Noemi assists in maintaining open communication with engineers, operations staff, data center representatives, Account Managers, Management Team and clients.  Furthermore, she assists in the provision of formal reports and services summaries to document milestone services and/or service impacting changes.  In parallel to the client services, Noemi is also engaged in managing multiple internal projects and initiatives, among them the execution of scheduled maintenance services, the refinement of the support escalation process, adjustment of the emergency support line, etc., and communicating progress to the cloud team.

As part of the service coordination, Noemi created the service contracts, processed executed contracts, scheduled the execution of services and confirmed service completion with contracts.  During this time, Noemi assisted in integrating the resources and establishing processes to increase efficiency in invoicing, communication, deliverable creation and project management.

This global institution worked with Asperitas to replicate its on-premises network to simulate, test, and deploy multiple enhancements to their entire global network.  This project was focused on leveraging a Network Digital Twin for replicating, simulating, testing, automating, and deploying a global cloud-based VPN for better overall user experience around the world for 20,000+ users.
SCOPE OF WORK 
During the project the teams looked at the overall implementation of the Network Digital Twin with several keys to ensuring a successful overall deployment of the cloud-based VPN service.  The Digital Twin replicated the entire global network including data centers, WAN, SD-WAN and remote locations. The Network Digital Twin was tasked with simulating; network routing, network advertisements, regional IPSec connectivity, regional network failures, etc.

RESULT 
The customer’s hosted deployment of Network Digital Twin resulted in improved speed to market and lowered business risk.  Using automation and proprietary software the customer was able to see acceleration in their development process.  The change performed inside of this project took 3 months instead of the 2 years that the customer had originally planned without the use of the Network Digital Twin.  Additionally, they were able to reduce production deployment errors by identifying them in the Network Digital Twin before deploying them in production. The customer has had zero production deployment errors for all automated deployments.

about: Hi, I'm Mere! I am a meaning maker, visualizer, and storyteller who is fueled by creativity, motivated by connection, and excited by innovation. At Deloitte, I have designed immersive experiences focused on what matters most to executives and their teams, used design thinking to diagnose challenges and elicit ah-has, created an offering to bring the power and delight of visual storytelling to clients, and launched new assets that instill wonder.

experience.description: I am a manager in Deloitte Next Gen Delivery, the team responsible for exploring, assessing, and integrating next-generation space, technology, and content to shape and accelerate the future of client experiences at Deloitte. I co-created and managed the strategy to launch the Chicago Next Gen Greenhouse, including the branding, events, marketing, and communications. Powered by cutting-edge technology, including an immersive dome, augmented reality (AR)/virtual reality (VR), hologram, and digital twin technology, the Chicago Next Gen Greenhouse is an immersive, interactive asset that inspires teams to unlock and accelerate innovation and break through complex challenges.

experience.position: Offering Manager, Experience Design and Innovation at the Deloitte Greenhouse
experience.description:
The Deloitte Greenhouse hosts Labs for Deloitte teams, client teams, and mixed groups that want to step outside business as usual to tackle complex challenges. Based on insights from more than 8,000 sessions with business leaders, The Deloitte Greenhouse Breakthrough Labs are rooted in powerful science and research from the fields of group dynamics, environmental psychology, design thinking, and innovation theory. The Greenhouse takes problem solving to a new level by engaging leaders intellectually, physically, and emotionally. 

In my role as Lead Digital Artist, I specialize in Graphic Capture (also referred to as Graphic Recording), the real-time synthesis of conversation into hand-drawn visuals, captured digitally on iPad. I create deliverables for clients to transform noise into insights, distraction into engagement, and complex content into digestible stories. With over five years of experience producing and managing Greenhouse Labs, I am able to visually synthesize conversations across any industry, from highly technical conversations to deeply sensitive teaming discussions. I manage the National Graphic Capture offering and support creative pursuits across the Greenhouse, including the revamp and deployment of the Greenhouse Visual Identity and training of practitioners in visual synthesis skills.  I continue to manage Deloitte Greenhouse Breakthrough Labs.

I am based in Chicago, but support all six Greenhouse sites in Chicago, Dallas, DC, Houston, New York, and San Francisco.

publications.title: Quantifying the Uniqueness of Donald Trump in Presidential Discourse
publications.description:
Does Donald Trump speak differently from other presidents? If so, in what ways? Are these
differences confined to any single medium of communication? To investigate these questions,
this paper introduces a novel metric of uniqueness based on large language models, develops
a new lexicon for divisive speech, and presents a framework for comparing the lexical features
of political opponents. Applying these tools to a variety of corpora of presidential speeches, we
find considerable evidence that Trump’s speech patterns diverge from those of all major party
nominees for the presidency in recent history. Some notable findings include Trump’s employment
of particularly divisive and antagonistic language targeting of his political opponents and his
patterns of repetition for emphasis. Furthermore, Trump is significantly more distinctive than his
fellow Republicans, whose uniqueness values are comparably closer to those of the Democrats.
These differences hold across a variety of measurement strategies, arise on both the campaign
trail and in official presidential addresses, and do not appear to be an artifact of secular time
trends.

publications.title: Uprooting or Sowing Violence?: Coca Eradication and Guerrilla Violence in Colombia
publications.description: Belligerent nonstate actors including terrorist organizations often exploit illicit economies to fund their activities. In Colombia numerous belligerent groups are involved in illegal narcotics markets. For more than 20 years, the Colombian government has responded with targeted eradication of illicit crops, intending to undermine the groups' sources of revenue while simultaneously disrupting the illicit drug economy. Despite its duration, this policy's effect on guerrilla violence remains unclear. Examining the potential for violent backlash to these tactics, this research note assesses the impact of aerial coca crop eradication in Colombia from 2004–2005 on domestic Colombian guerrilla kidnappings, assassinations, and terrorism.

publications.title: Topic Modeling Quiet Quitting and Antiwork Through the Lens of Motivation Theory
publications.publishedAt: Society for Industrial and Organizational Psychology Annual Conference, Chicago, IL, United States. · Apr 17, 2024
publications.description: Quiet quitting and antiwork are explored through Herzberg’s two-factor theory (1959). Topic modeling of Reddit threads indicates that both quiet quitters and antiworkers report a greater proportion of issues with hygiene factors than motivation factors in their comments. Quiet quitters also comment on a greater proportion of motivation factors than antiworkers, while antiworkers comment on a greater proportion of hygiene factors. The academic and practical implications regarding quiet quitting/intrinsic factors and antiwork/extrinsic factors are discussed.

publications.title: In These Unprecedented Times: Human Centered Approaches to Continuous Change
publications.publishedAt: Society for Industrial and Organizational Psychology Annual Conference, Boston, MA, United States. · Apr 20, 2023
publications.description: This master tutorial provides attendees with an introductory-level knowledge of change fatigue and how a human-centered approach can be utilized when addressing symptoms. Authors delve into traditional ways organizational leaders may address change fatigue and postulate that many causes of rapid changes in the workplace could be the result of traumatic events, such as the global pandemic. They then introduce how Trauma-Informed Care, adopted from the social work and clinical psychology practices as a new lens through which organizational change and change management could be viewed.

Reviewed blueprint documentation and then worked with large implementation team to complete the configuration. Heavily involved with the go live process verifying all transports had been completed in order.  Involved in customer acceptance activities prior to go live.  

After go live for this client on January 2010, was responsible for all payroll runs made by ACS.  This included the training of the operation staff in Dallas, TX and Monterrey, MX.  Was also responsible for the activities of three contractors and two in house employees in the Dallas office doing support work including additional reporting, updating of inbound and outbound files, new configuration work and documenting the existing system.

August 2009 to October 2009
Was assigned to support the go live for a large electronics firm. Required extensive tax work with the client for PA locals and wage type configuration issues.  Worked with the development team in gathering additional requirements after go live.  He spent a lot of time at the client location training staff on payroll tax assignments and providing support with end users of the system.

June 2008 to August 2009
Senior Lead Consultant for the implementation of SAP Payroll for a large oil and gas company.  Responsible for all phases of payroll development from blueprint updates through configuration and implementation. Was responsible for the work of twelve contractors and employees on the account.  Developed requirements for additional sub schemas and rules that were added to the basic SAP system.  He was heavily involved in user meetings and design requirements.

Took over as the project lead for an SAP HCM implementation for an oil and gas exploration company.  Was responsible for all phases of the implementation.  Was also responsible for all configuration of the payroll portion of the implementation.  Developed additional rules for the payroll schema to match the stated needs of the client.  Implemented all the BSI software and installed all BSI tax updates.  Installed and trained user on the use of BSI Tax Factory.

One of the Senior Consultants on a large public sector implementation for a state on the east coast.  Was involved in upfront user meetings to set requirements for the project.  Was part of team putting together the blueprint documentation.  Responsible for training client in the payroll configuration of wage types, BSI Tax Factory, features, rules and schema modification.  Worked with benefits team in the configuration of benefits from the payroll side with deduction models and reporting. Was involved with the development of inbound and outbound interfaces to the benefit providers.

January 2005 to March 2005
Was assigned to an ongoing project with a large university while waiting for the start of the state project.  Worked with the staff on wage type review and user training.  Also helped develop additional rules for payroll processing.

Brought into project for an insurance company to help get project back on schedule for a December go live.  Took over most configuration including wage types, rules, schema and updates to features. Was responsible for testing and the loading of YTD data for parallel testing using schema ULK9.  Worked with client and other team members for parallel testing and issue resolution.  Was instrumental in helping users in selection of equipment for post payroll processing.

Bought the SAP practice from marchFIRST.

Competed blueprint phase for a global HR system out of the Netherlands.  He was responsible as project manager for four other consultants working on PA, OM, Comp Management.  Was personally responsible for the ADP interface for Payroll and master data changes using Idoc’s and ADP Connection.  He reviewed ADP’s GlobalView SAP system for possible use in the future.

Was brought in to bring an implementation back on schedule for go live at a medical hospital group.  Duties included configuration of payroll, schema changes, writing additional rules and user training.  Gave special instruction on the use of the BSI Tax Factory software for multi company setup to end users.

Was responsible for all aspects of an HR/Payroll system for a manufacturing company implementing the whole suite of SAP products.  Responsibilities included all Gross to Net payroll activities, interfacing Kronos Time System into SAP infotypes for attendances and absences that were then assigned to base pay, overtime, shift premium, taxation and other wage types.  Was responsible for benefits integration that required new configuration on a completely new vendor with different insurance coverage’s.  Responsible for all conversion and go live activities.  Produced all documentation for all areas within HR/Payroll.  Was the consultant in charge of all client training activities.  Was called in as subject matter experts at different times for other activities including Organizational Structure and specialized rules for time loading and time evaluation.

Responsible for implementation of the US Payroll for a large multi-national food processing company.  Activities included net payroll processing, wage types, garnishments, tax computation, benefits integration, deductions with models and implementation of interfaces for printing checks/direct deposits and tax reporting to ADP.   
.
Responsible for repairing a system from errors in the loading of historical data.  Errors were not detected until after two payrolls had been run and posted.  The system required extensive reconfiguration.  Incorrect balances were loaded for 401k and Employee Stock Purchase Plan.  These items had to be recalculated using spreadsheets in order to get correct balances to report to third party administrator.    

Audited and reconfigured an existing payroll implementation.  Corrected processing errors and made necessary changes to payroll schema.  Aided the client manager in correcting general ledger from manual postings to SAP posting of each payroll.  Installed the newly required tables for processing Canadian Worker’s Compensation, and performed additional training for user in the use of the Payroll System. 

Implemented a gross to net payroll for a company of about 2,000 employees.  Responsible for project management of other consultants for time, ADP tax interface and net configuration.  Personally responsible for portions of the configuration, problem resolution and writing of special payroll rules to meet special needs of client. Worked closely with other consultants integrating SAP’s FI/CO module for banking, third party remittance including garnishment and check processing.

Responsible for the review of an existing payroll implementation. System required modifications for gross payroll processing for file sent to ADP.  Modifications were also necessary for deductions and deduction models to be workable in the future years.  Worked closely with Payroll Manager in resolving payroll issues of employees and FI/CO postings.

Senior Payroll Consultant for the implementation of payroll for a utility company.  This included the full implementation of all aspects of payroll.  Lead team effort for the payroll and parallel testing.

Participated as a member of the SAP team for this 5000 employee state school population and performed a review of the entire payroll implementation including, but not limited to, the following areas: Wage types, retro calculations of payroll, configuration of tax reporter, resolving issues with working with multiple pay periods, off cycle processing and reconciling FI/CO YTD and the W2’s that were issued.  

Implemented SAP Payroll for a mutual funds company with 1200 employees in over 20 locations.  Responsible for all areas of Payroll configuration including taxation, benefits integration, transfer to FI/CO, wage type development, off cycle processing, month end accruals, banking and third party remittances for benefits, taxes and other vendor payments.  Additional responsibilities included teaching payroll to the rest of the team as well as client personnel.

Was one of two consultants in charge of implementing SAP payroll for a manufacturing company in Chicago.  Areas of concentration were wage types, taxes, benefits integration, FI/CO interface, off cycle, third party remittances, deductions, data medium exchange and month end accruals.

Retained by SAP America to teach the Gross and Net Payroll classes.  Taught in New Jersey, Chicago, Dallas, Philadelphia and San Francisco.  The two classes encompass all of the basic information for configuration of payroll.  Review of classroom material and the Implementation Guide (IMG) are used to teach the student both theory and practice of SAP’s R/3 North American Payroll System.
